result.title: Does Multi-Agent Collaboration Reduce Hallucination in Clinical Tasks?
result.summary: Multi-agent LLM systems improve performance on clinical tasks, and that improvement is often read as evidence of a more trustworthy system. However, the two are not the same claim. A clinician acts on the stated reasoning and not only on the conclusion, so whether collaboration reduces hallucination, and what decides when it does, has to be measured in the reasoning too. Yet most evaluations score only the final answer. We evaluate four systems (a single-LLM baseline and three multi-agent topologies) across four models and three clinical tasks, scoring hallucination, under a factuality and faithfulness taxonomy, inside the rationale each system generates and reporting it alongside the task metric. We report that collaboration buys task performance but not lower hallucination as a rule, and no topology is reliably better than another. The effect differs by model: of the $36$ model--system--task comparisons, $12$ are large enough to resolve --- four decreases and eight increases, with no model on both sides. What sets the level, and the direction of any change, is the model rather than the topology or the number of agents. A self-correction experiment is consistent with this: shown its own flagged errors, every model except Llama-3.2-3B-Instruct reduces hallucination; the one model for which collaboration lowers hallucination gains the most, and Llama-3.2-3B-Instruct, the model whose hallucination it amplifies most, does not reduce its hallucination at all. We find that collaboration redistributes what its models can already do; it does not supply what they cannot.

AI.brief_summary: 论文在四个模型、三个临床任务上比较单 LLM 基线与三种多智能体拓扑，按事实性与忠实性分类法对生成理由内部的幻觉打分并结合任务指标，另做自纠错实验，发现协作能提升任务表现但不必然降低幻觉，模型而非拓扑决定幻觉水平与变化方向。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「在 rationale 层面而非仅最终答案打分」及给予自身标记错误的纠错协议，可能为核查 LVR 中 latent 内容是否真被答案使用、多路径推理的错误归因提供方法线索；但无视觉输入与 latent 状态，属远距离借鉴。
